about: Book introductions: short orientation, optional “fight,” anchor verses, and a small step. KJV-only site; human tone.

Genesis.summary: Creation, fall, and promise: God keeps covenant when people fail. The long war between faith and self-rule starts here.
Genesis.fight: Who is God, who are we, and what promise outlasts the fall? The fight is faith versus self-rule.
Genesis.step: Trace one promise from Genesis 12 to Genesis 50 in a single sitting—watch God’s covenant stay steadier than His people.

Exodus.summary: Rescue and law: God hears the cry of the burdened and teaches a freed people how to walk with Him.

Leviticus.summary: Holiness in daily life: sacrifice, purity, and nearness to God—grace and boundary for a camp at war with sin.

Numbers.summary: Wilderness years: grumbling versus trust; God stays faithful through forty years of testing.

Deuteronomy.summary: Second law, same heart: remember what God did, choose life, teach the next generation before battle.

Joshua.summary: Taking ground: courage, obedience, and one generation that must decide whom they will serve.

Judges.summary: Cycles of compromise: when everyone does what is right in their own eyes, God still raises deliverers.

Ruth.summary: Loyalty and redemption: ordinary faithfulness in famine; God weaves a Moabitess into the line of the King.

1 Samuel.summary: Kingship begins: God’s prophet, a flawed king, and the search for a heart after God.

2 Samuel.summary: David’s reign: triumph, sin, and consequence—grace that does not erase accountability.

1 Kings.summary: Temple and split: wisdom, idolatry, and the question of who is really on the throne.

2 Kings.summary: Prophets and exile: last chances, judgment, and the hope that God is not finished with His people.

1 Chronicles.summary: Genealogy and worship: Israel’s story retold for those who need to remember who they are.

2 Chronicles.summary: Kings and temple: revival, pride, and exile—God’s eyes still run to and fro the earth.

Ezra.summary: Return and rebuild: Scripture read again; holiness and courage after shame.

Nehemiah.summary: Walls and hearts: prayer, work, and opposition—leadership that weeps then acts.

Esther.summary: Hidden providence: no verse names God, yet deliverance for His people is unmistakable.

Job.summary: Suffering and silence: friends miss the mark; God answers out of the whirlwind, not the courtroom.

Psalm.summary: Prayer book for battle: lament, trust, thanks, and kingship—honest words for honest days.
Psalm.fight: How to talk with God when you are afraid, angry, glad, or numb—training for real life with Him.
Psalm.step: Pick one psalm that fits your mood today, read it aloud slowly, then pray one line back to God.

Proverbs.summary: Wisdom for the path: fear of the Lord first; practical sense for mouth, money, and neighbor.
Proverbs.fight: The fear of the Lord first—then wisdom for mouth, money, and neighbor in a loud world.
Proverbs.step: Read the Proverbs chapter that matches today’s date; circle one verse to obey before sunset.

Ecclesiastes.summary: Vanity under the sun: life without God as center is smoke; fear God and keep His commandments.

Song of Solomon.summary: Love and desire: covenant affection within God’s order; read also as echo of God and His people.

Isaiah.summary: Judgment and comfort: holy King, suffering Servant, new creation—light for nations in darkness.

Jeremiah.summary: Tears and truth: a prophet who loves the city God must discipline; a new covenant on the heart.

Lamentations.summary: Grief in ruins: honest sorrow after fall; yet “great is thy faithfulness” still stands.

Ezekiel.summary: Glory and exile: visions of God’s presence leaving and returning; hearts of stone to hearts of flesh.

Daniel.summary: Faith in empire: prayer when law forbids it; God rules the beasts and the years.

Hosea.summary: Unfaithful love: God’s steadfastness to a people who play the harlot; mercy over sacrifice.

Joel.summary: Day of the Lord: locusts, repentance, and Spirit poured out—wake up before it is too late.

Amos.summary: Justice for the poor: worship without righteousness is noise; let justice run down as waters.

Obadiah.summary: Pride of Edom: God judges those who gloat over Jacob’s hurt; the kingdom belongs to the Lord.

Jonah.summary: Mercy beyond borders: a prophet who runs; Nineveh repents; God cares for cattle and city alike.

Micah.summary: Do justly, love mercy: small-town prophet; Bethlehem named; God pardons the remnant.

Nahum.summary: Nineveh’s fall: God is slow to anger but not soft on cruelty; comfort for the oppressed.

Habakkuk.summary: Why evil prospers: faith that waits though the fig tree fails; joy in the God who saves.

Zephaniah.summary: Day near at hand: silence before God; joy for the humble remnant when the King reigns.

Haggai.summary: Rebuild the house: post-exile lethargy; God’s glory worth more than paneled homes.

Zechariah.summary: Visions and branches: return, cleanse, and look—your King comes lowly on a colt.

Malachi.summary: Covenant weariness: “Wherein hast thou loved us?” God answers; Elijah’s spirit before the great day.

Matthew.summary: Kingdom of heaven: Jesus as promised King, teacher, and sacrifice—God with us to the end.
Matthew.fight: Kingdom of heaven versus anxiety, performance, and the need to look righteous—Jesus goes for the heart first.
Matthew.step: Read Matthew 5–7 across a week (one chapter a day) and mark one command that names you kindly.

Mark.summary: Servant who rushes: immediacy, cross before crown; who do men say that I am?

Luke.summary: Son of Man for outsiders: mercy, meals, and a journey to Jerusalem for the world’s life.

John.summary: Believe: signs point to the Word made flesh; life in His name for those who trust.
John.fight: Believing Jesus is the Christ—life in His name instead of a religion you manufacture.
John.step: Read John 3–4 and notice who believes; ask the Lord to show you one person to pray for by name.

Acts.summary: Witness in power: the Spirit spreads the church from Jerusalem to Rome—doors open, stones fly.

Romans.summary: Gospel unpacked: wrath, grace, union with Christ, one body—obedience from faith for all nations.
Romans.fight: Who is right with God, and how does that change the way we walk? Paul speaks to the conscience.
Romans.step: Read Romans 5:1–11 and underline every “we” or “us” that speaks of union with Christ.

1 Corinthians.summary: Church in a city: cross-shaped wisdom, body life, love that never fails.
1 Corinthians.fight: Cross-shaped wisdom where the city loves status and noise—love that never fails when gifts do not.
1 Corinthians.step: Read 1 Corinthians 13:4–7 aloud; underline one line that corrects you—pray it for your church.

2 Corinthians.summary: Weakness as strength: Paul’s thorn; treasure in earthen vessels; reconciliation ministry.
2 Corinthians.fight: Comfort in affliction first—then pour it out; God’s strength lands in cracked jars, not polished speeches.
2 Corinthians.step: Read 2 Corinthians 1:3–7 slowly—thank God for one way He comforted you that you can pass on to someone else this week.

Galatians.summary: Freedom: not circumcision but faith working through love—stand fast in liberty.

Ephesians.summary: Seated with Christ: one new man, armor for the long war, prayer for all saints.
Ephesians.fight: From dead in sins to seated with Christ—unity in the body and armor for the long war.
Ephesians.step: Memorize one short phrase from Ephesians 6:10–18 this week; say it before a hard conversation.

Philippians.summary: Joy in chains: Christ magnified in life or death; mind of humility as His.
Philippians.fight: Joy in chains and thorns—Christ is enough when feelings are not; humility and prayer beat performance.
Philippians.step: Philippians 4:6–8—name one worry, pray with thanks, then pick one “whatsoever things” from verse 8 to rehearse today. Open Battle Plans for verse-led tracks that draw on Philippians.

Colossians.summary: Fullness in Christ: not philosophy or rule; put off old man, put on love which binds.

1 Thessalonians.summary: Hope of His coming: dead in Christ rise first; comfort one another with these words.

2 Thessalonians.summary: Steadfast under rumor: don’t be shaken; pray God counts you worthy of His calling.

1 Timothy.summary: Order in the house: faithful sayings, widows, elders—fight the good fight.

2 Timothy.summary: Last charge: Scripture God-breathed; endure hardship; crown laid up.

Titus.summary: Sound doctrine on Crete: older saints, younger saints, grace that teaches sober living.

Philemon.summary: Onesimus: gospel rewrites a slave letter; love beyond what is required.

Hebrews.summary: Better: Christ over angels, Moses, priesthood—draw near, hold fast, stir up love.
Hebrews.fight: Will you drift from Christ, or draw near to a Priest who sat down because the work finished?
Hebrews.step: Read Hebrews 10:19–25 aloud and pick one “let us” to obey before the week ends.

James.summary: Faith that works: trials, tongue, care for widows—show me thy faith without works.
James.fight: Faith that shows in the tongue, the pocket, and the widow’s row—not empty words.
James.step: James 1:5—ask God for wisdom for one concrete decision you face this week.

1 Peter.summary: Strangers scattered: suffering honorably; hope living in fearful hearts.
1 Peter.fight: Holy living in exile when the world mislabels you—honor without fear; hope under fire.
1 Peter.step: Name one care you rehearse in your mind; pray 1 Peter 5:7 slowly, then leave it with God in one written sentence.

2 Peter.summary: Remember: false teachers, day of the Lord, grow in grace and knowledge.

1 John.summary: Know you have life: light, love, spirit of antichrist—believe on the Son.

2 John.summary: Walk in truth: do not bid false teachers God speed—love with discernment.

3 John.summary: Hospitality and Diotrephes: support those who go forth for the name.

Jude.summary: Contend once delivered: examples of judgment; keep in God’s love.

Revelation.summary: Jesus wins: letters, seals, trumpets, King of kings—no more curse; come, Lord Jesus.
Revelation.fight: Jesus is Lord over empire, fear, and the final lie—so hold fast until He comes.
Revelation.step: Read one letter to the churches in Revelation 2–3; ask what Jesus says to small, tired congregations.
